elements.form: λαβόμενος τοῦ ἱματίου ἄνωθεν αὐτοῦ παρὰ τὸν ὦμον

signals.observation: Polemarchus' physical intervention is narrated through a dense sequence of bodily actions: extending the hand, grasping the cloak at the shoulder, drawing Adeimantus toward himself, leaning forward, and bending close to whisper.

elements.context: Ἀφήσομεν οὖν, ἔφη, ἢ τί δράσομεν;
καθαρός γε καὶ ἐκεῖ ὁ ἀφεθείς

signals.observation: ἀφίημι recurs across the section: first as the question whether to let Socrates go (ἀφήσομεν), then Socrates asking why they won't release him (οὐκ ἀφίετε), then Glaucon releasing him as from a homicide charge (ἀφίεμέν σε), and finally the acquitted person (ὁ ἀφεθείς).
ἀφίημι shifts from the context of releasing Socrates from the conversation to acquitting him of homicide—the same verb moves from detention to legal absolution.

Forms of λαμβάνω/ἐπιλαμβάνω cluster: Polemarchus physically grasps (λαβόμενος) Adeimantus' cloak, Socrates is accused of grasping at another constitution (ἐπιλαμβάνῃ), and Socrates says they have seized hold of him (ἐπιλαβόμενοί μου).

elements.context: εἶδος ὅλον οὐ τὸ ἐλάχιστον ἐκκλέπτειν τοῦ λόγου

signals.observation: Adeimantus accuses Socrates of laziness (ἀπορρᾳθυμεῖν), stealing away a whole form of the argument (ἐκκλέπτειν), and thinking he would escape notice (λήσειν)—a local cluster of evasion and concealment.

elements.context: ἀγαθὴν μὲν τοίνυν τὴν τοιαύτην πόλιν τε καὶ πολιτείαν καὶ ὀρθὴν καλῶ
ὀρθὴ παίδων τε καὶ γυναικῶν κτῆσίς τε καὶ χρεία

signals.observation: ὀρθός recurs throughout: applied first to the city and constitution, then questioned by Adeimantus (τὸ ὀρθῶς τοῦτο... λόγου δεῖται), then to the community of women and children as right or not right, and finally to the correct possession and use of women and children.

elements.context: τίς ἡ κοινωνία τοῖς φύλαξιν ἡμῖν

signals.observation: The κοινός family recurs densely: the proverb κοινὰ τὰ φίλων, the manner of κοινωνία questioned twice, Glaucon making himself κοινωνός of the vote, and the final restatement of the guardians' κοινωνία.

elements.context: ἢ ἀπατεῶνα καλῶν τε καὶ ἀγαθῶν

signals.observation: Socrates introduces an analogy between involuntary homicide and intellectual deception; Glaucon picks it up by acquitting Socrates as from homicide (ὥσπερ φόνου) and declaring him clean (καθαρόν) and no deceiver (μὴ ἀπατεῶνα).

ἀπιστ- forms cluster densely: Socrates says the topic holds many grounds for disbelief (ἀπιστίας), would be disbelieved on possibility (ἀπιστοῖτʼ) and on desirability (ἀπιστήσεται); Glaucon assures the audience is not ἄπιστοι; Socrates describes himself as ἀπιστοῦντα—distrusting his own knowledge.

Socrates contrasts speaking with confidence among friends who know (ἀσφαλές, θαρραλέον) against speaking while doubting and seeking (φοβερόν, σφαλερόν); παραθαρρύνειν names what Glaucon attempts but Socrates says achieves the opposite.

elements.context: πρὶν ἂν ταῦτα πάντα ὥσπερ τἆλλα διέλθῃς

signals.observation: διέρχομαι recurs as the central verb of argumentative traversal: Socrates is accused of avoiding it, commanded to complete it, was glad to think it done, and now says it is not easy.
The proverbial phrase κοινὰ τὰ φίλων is cited as what Socrates tried to pass off casually (εἰπὼν αὐτὸ φαύλως), applied specifically to women and children.
σφάλλω recurs three times in close proximity: the danger is σφαλερόν, the fear is σφαλεὶς τῆς ἀληθείας, and the subject is one where one must least σφάλλεσθαι.

elements.context: ἐν γὰρ φρονίμοις τε καὶ φίλοις
τῶν μεγίστων τε καὶ φίλων τἀληθῆ

signals.observation: φίλος recurs across shifting contexts: the proverb about friends' property, addressing the interlocutor as φίλε ἑταῖρε, speaking among wise friends, dragging friends down in error, and the claim that risking error is better among enemies than among friends.
Socrates invokes Adrasteia (Nemesis) before speaking, a ritual gesture of propitiation against the consequences of what he is about to say.

elements.context: μετὰ ἀνδρεῖον δρᾶμα παντελῶς διαπερανθὲν τὸ γυναικεῖον αὖ περαίνειν

signals.observation: Socrates frames the argument as a sequence of dramatic acts: after the male drama (ἀνδρεῖον δρᾶμα) is fully completed, the female one (τὸ γυναικεῖον) must now be carried through.
Socrates describes the arguments they are stirring up as a swarm (ἑσμόν) of words, which he had previously let pass (παρῆκα).

elements.context: χρυσοχοήσοντας οἴει τούσδε νῦν ἐνθάδε ἀφῖχθαι

signals.observation: Thrasymachus asks sarcastically whether Socrates thinks they have come to smelt gold rather than hear arguments—a striking hapax-like word introducing a concrete trade as foil to λόγων ἀκουσομένους.

elements.context: μέτρον δέ γʼ... τοιούτων λόγων ἀκούειν ὅλος ὁ βίος

signals.observation: Socrates says the arguments should be moderate (μετρίων); Glaucon redefines the measure (μέτρον) as a whole lifetime of listening.

elements.context: ὧν ἄλλο μὲν οὐδὲν κατηκούσαμεν, τόδε δέ

signals.observation: The narration specifies that of Polemarchus' whispered words, only one phrase was overheard (κατηκούσαμεν)—the question Ἀφήσομεν οὖν, ἢ τί δράσομεν emerges from partial audibility.

elements.context: ἃ τότε ἴσως ἔδει ἐφεξῆς λέγειν

signals.observation: Socrates was about to describe constitutions transitioning in sequence (ἐφεξῆς... μεταβαίνειν); at the section's end he acknowledges he must now say in reverse order (ἀνάπαλιν) what perhaps should have been said ἐφεξῆς—the planned sequence is disrupted.

elements.context: ὡς ἀγέλης φύλακας τοὺς ἄνδρας καθιστάναι τῷ λόγῳ

signals.observation: Socrates recalls that they established the men as guardians of a flock (ἀγέλης φύλακας), an image now being extended to the genesis and rearing of offspring.

elements.context: μὴ εὐχὴ δοκῇ εἶναι ὁ λόγος

signals.observation: Socrates expresses reluctance (ὄκνος) to engage the topic lest the argument appear to be a mere prayer (εὐχή) rather than a demonstrable logos.
The female/male pairing shifts from guardian dogs (θηλείας/ἄρρενες) to women/men (γυναιξίν/ἀνδράσι) and back to θήλεια/ἄρρενος applied to human nature.

elements.context: τὸ ἐν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς δὴ γελοῖον ἐξερρύη
γελοῖον ἄλλο τι ἡγεῖται ἢ τὸ κακόν
πρὸς ἄλλην τινὰ ὄψιν ἀποβλέπων ὡς γελοίου

signals.observation: γελοῖος recurs densely, shifting from what appears ridiculous (visual impression) to a redefinition where only τὸ κακόν is truly γελοῖον.
The γυμνός/γυμνάσιον lexical family recurs densely, linking nakedness to exercise for both women and men.
Stripping (ἀποδύεσθαι) and covering up (συγκαλύπτειν) are set in direct contrast as alternatives.

elements.context: τὸ ἐν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς δὴ γελοῖον
ὑπὸ τοῦ ἐν τοῖς λόγοις μηνυθέντος ἀρίστου

signals.observation: The ridiculous in the eyes (ὀφθαλμοῖς) is displaced by the best revealed in speech (λόγοις).

elements.context: τῇ τοῦ ἄρρενος γένους κοινωνῆσαι εἰς ἅπαντα τὰ ἔργα

signals.observation: κοινῇ appears twice in the dog analogy and its application; κοινωνῆσαι returns when the question is restated about human nature.

elements.context: τὸν τῶν σκυλάκων τόκον τε καὶ τροφήν
τὴν αὐτὴν τροφήν τε καὶ παιδείαν
τῶν γυναικῶν καὶ παίδων κτῆσιν καὶ τροφήν

signals.observation: τροφή appears first as rearing of puppies, then as training of animals generally, then as rearing of women and children.
Weaker (ἀσθενεστέραις) and stronger (ἰσχυροτέροις) are set as comparative contrasts within shared work.
Staying indoors (οἰκουρεῖν ἔνδον) is contrasted with co-guarding (συμφυλάττειν) and co-hunting (συνθηρεύειν), both prefixed with συν-.

elements.context: τοῖς Ἕλλησιν ἐδόκει αἰσχρὰ εἶναι καὶ γελοῖα

signals.observation: Past Greek attitudes to male nakedness are compared to present barbarian attitudes.
Cretans first, then Spartans, in the sequence of peoples who began exercising naked.

elements.context: δυνατὴ φύσις ἡ ἀνθρωπίνη ἡ θήλεια
πάμπολυ διαφέρει γυνὴ ἀνδρὸς τὴν φύσιν
κατὰ φύσιν ἕκαστον ἕνα ἓν τὸ αὑτοῦ πράττειν

signals.observation: φύσις recurs five times in the self-objection passage (453a-c), pivoting the argument on whether different nature requires different work.
Socrates proposes giving room for dispute and then takes up the opposing argument himself on behalf of others.
Mockery is named through σκώμματα, κωμῳδεῖν, and γελωτοποιεῖν in close proximity.

elements.form: πορευτέον πρὸς τὸ τραχὺ τοῦ νόμου

signals.observation: Having set out to speak (ὡρμήσαμεν, ἠρξάμεθα) is twice invoked as reason to press on toward the rough part of the law.

elements.context: γελοῖον ἄλλο τι ἡγεῖται ἢ τὸ κακόν

signals.observation: κακόν is the only proper object of ridicule; καλόν and ἀγαθόν are the proper standards for serious pursuit, set in contrast.

elements.context: ἵνα μὴ ἔρημα τὰ τοῦ ἑτέρου λόγου πολιορκῆται

signals.observation: The opposing argument is described as besieged (πολιορκῆται) and undefended (ἔρημα), a military image within a discussion partly about women sharing in war.
A cluster of swimming and sea language: small pool, open sea, swimming, the verbal adjective νευστέον, rescue by dolphin, and σῴζεσθαι, all concentrated in 453d.
Forms of ἐπιτηδεύω/ἐπιτήδευμα recur throughout the section with high density, appearing in nearly every stage of the argument.

elements.context: τῆς ἑτέρας τε καὶ τῆς αὐτῆς φύσεως
ἑτέρα φύσις γυναικός τε καὶ ἀνδρός
ἡ αὐτὴ φύσις εἰς φυλακὴν πόλεως

signals.observation: φύσις recurs pervasively, repeatedly qualified as αὐτή or ἑτέρα/ἄλλη, tracking the argument's pivot on what counts as same or different nature.

elements.context: ἔριδι, οὐ διαλέκτῳ πρὸς ἀλλήλους χρώμενοι

signals.observation: ἔρις/ἐρίζειν and διαλέγεσθαι/διάλεκτος are set in explicit contrast twice at 454a; ἐριστικῶς returns at 454b applied to the speakers' own procedure.

elements.context: τί εἶδος τῆς ἑτέρας τε καὶ τῆς αὐτῆς φύσεως
ἐκεῖνο τὸ εἶδος τῆς ἀλλοιώσεώς τε καὶ ὁμοιώσεως

signals.observation: εἶδος and ὄνομα are contrasted as modes of inquiry: pursuing by name (κατʼ ὄνομα διώκειν) versus examining by εἶδος (κατʼ εἴδη διαιρούμενοι). ὄνομα recurs at 454b applied reflexively.
Three forms from the ἀντιλέγω family appear across 454a–455a, marking the practice the argument identifies and then turns against.
μικράν and μέγιστον are placed in direct contrast as the two bodies of water.
The bald/long-haired pair is introduced as a reductio: their difference is acknowledged as ἐναντία yet its application to cobbling is called γελοῖον.

elements.context: ἰατρικὸν μὲν καὶ ἰατρικὴν τὴν ψυχὴν ὄντα
τῶν ποπάνων τε καὶ ἑψημάτων θεραπείαν

signals.observation: Concrete crafts and domestic arts are cited as illustrative cases: cobbling, medicine, carpentry, weaving, cakes, and stews.

elements.context: τὸ εἶδος τῆς ἀλλοιώσεώς τε καὶ ὁμοιώσεως

signals.observation: ἀλλοίωσις and ὁμοίωσις are paired as the relevant εἶδος of difference and likeness that should govern the inquiry.
The male-female biological difference is reduced to two infinitives—τίκτειν and ὀχεύειν—explicitly marked as insufficient to establish relevant difference for ἐπιτηδεύματα.
ἀσθενής appears twice in comparative form at the conclusion, paired with ἰσχυροτέρα, as the sole conceded difference within shared nature.

elements.context: τὸν μὲν εὐφυῆ πρός τι εἶναι

signals.observation: A series of paired opposites (εὐφυής/ἀφυής, φιλόσοφος/μισόσοφος, θυμοειδής/ἄθυμος, πολεμική/ἀπόλεμος, γυμναστική/φιλογυμναστική) structures the enumeration of capacities that women may or may not share.
The φυλακ- family concentrates at the argument's conclusion (456a–b), applied to both women and men as the section reaches its result about guardian nature.

elements.context: εἰς αὐτὴν καὶ ἄκοντες πολλοὶ ἐμπίπτειν

signals.observation: ἐμπίπτω first describes falling into a pool of water at 453d and returns at 454a for falling into the antilogical art—both involve involuntary entry (ἄκοντες at 454a).

elements.context: ἥκομεν ἄρα εἰς τὰ πρότερα περιφερόμενοι

signals.observation: At 453e the search for an ἔξοδος (way out) is proposed; at 456b ἥκομεν announces arrival back at the prior position, completing the proposed movement through the argument.
ἄκοντες appears twice in close succession: first of many people falling unwillingly into antilogic, then applied reflexively to the speakers themselves.
Three συν-/συγ- compounds cluster at 456b (συνοικεῖν, συμφυλάττειν, συγγενεῖς), describing the joint life of men and women guardians.
The section's closing line negates two characterizations—impossible and wish-like—of what has been legislated.
σῴζω appears first as rescue from the argument's sea, then at 455b as retaining what one has learned—a shifted application of the same verb.

elements.context: παρὰ ταῦτα γιγνόμενα παρὰ φύσιν μᾶλλον

signals.observation: φύσις recurs three times; the first two are set in direct contrast (κατὰ φύσιν vs. παρὰ φύσιν), and the third applies the concept to the sameness of nature received by men and women.

elements.context: εἰ δυνατά γε καὶ βέλτιστα λέγοιμεν
ὅτι δὲ δὴ βέλτιστα, τὸ μετὰ τοῦτο δεῖ διομολογηθῆναι
οὐ μόνον ἄρα δυνατὸν ἀλλὰ καὶ ἄριστον

signals.observation: δυνατός and βέλτιστος are first paired, then separated into sequential stages of argument, then reunited at 457a where δυνατόν and ἄριστον are joined as accomplished.

elements.context: τὸν μὲν ἀμείνω ἄνδρα, τὸν δὲ χείρω
τῶν ἄλλων πολιτῶν οὐχ οὗτοι ἄριστοι
αἱ γυναῖκες τῶν γυναικῶν οὐχ αὗται ἔσονται βέλτισται
γυναῖκάς τε καὶ ἄνδρας ὡς ἀρίστους

signals.observation: Superlative and comparative forms of ἀγαθός accumulate densely, shifting from men alone (ἀμείνω, ἀμείνους, ἄριστοι) to women (βέλτισται) to both together (ἀρίστους) to the arrangement itself (ἄριστον).

elements.context: τὸν μὲν ἀμείνω ἄνδρα, τὸν δὲ χείρω

signals.observation: ἀμείνω and χείρω are placed in direct μέν/δέ contrast as better and worse man.

elements.context: οὐκ ἄλλη μὲν ἡμῖν ἄνδρας ποιήσει παιδεία

signals.observation: παιδεία/παιδεύω recurs, applied first to the single education for men and women, then to guardians' education, then contrastively to cobblers' training.

elements.context: ἢ τοὺς σκυτοτόμους, τῇ σκυτικῇ παιδευθέντας

signals.observation: Guardians and cobblers are set side by side as contrasting products of their respective educations; σκυτοτόμος and σκυτική cluster together.

elements.context: ἀποδυτέον δὴ ταῖς τῶν φυλάκων γυναιξίν

signals.observation: A cluster of undressing/clothing/nakedness: women must strip (ἀποδυτέον), will clothe themselves in virtue instead of garments (ἀρετὴν ἀντὶ ἱματίων ἀμφιέσονται), and appear naked (γυμναῖς) while exercising (γυμναζομέναις).
ἀρετή is placed as a substitute for ἱμάτια via ἀντί, contrasting virtue with garments.

elements.context: ὁ δὲ γελῶν ἀνὴρ ἐπὶ γυμναῖς γυναιξί
ἀτελῆ τοῦ γελοίου σοφίας δρέπων καρπόν

signals.observation: γελάω/γελοῖος appears four times; first as a casual remark about the question, then concentrated at 457b around the man who laughs at naked women, where laughing is characterized as harvesting an unripe fruit of the ridiculous.

elements.context: ἀτελῆ τοῦ γελοίου σοφίας δρέπων καρπόν

signals.observation: The man who laughs is said to pluck (δρέπων) an unripe fruit (ἀτελῆ καρπόν) of the ridiculous as wisdom (σοφίας)—a harvest image applied to laughter and knowledge.
A maxim pairs ὠφέλιμον with καλόν and βλαβερόν with αἰσχρόν in parallel μέν/δέ contrast.
κῦμα appears twice framing the wave image; κατακλυσθῆναι (being flooded) accompanies the first, and the second is called οὐ σμικρόν.
διομολογέω appears twice marking the two stages of agreement (possible, best), and ὁμολογέω closes the section describing the argument agreeing with itself.

elements.context: τῆς ἄλλης φυλακῆς τῆς περὶ τὴν πόλιν

signals.observation: The φύλαξ word-family recurs densely; φυλακίδας at 457c is a notable feminine coinage set beside φύλακας.

elements.context: τὰ ἐλαφρότερα ταῖς γυναιξὶν ἢ τοῖς ἀνδράσι δοτέον

signals.observation: Lighter tasks (ἐλαφρότερα) are assigned to women on account of the weakness (ἀσθένεια) of their sex, a qualification within the shared arrangement.

elements.context: κοινωνητέον πολέμου τε καὶ τῆς ἄλλης φυλακῆς

signals.observation: Four verbal adjectives in -τέον occur in rapid succession, each prescribing what must be done regarding guardian women.
Socrates says 'when you see' (ἴδῃς) the next wave, and the interlocutor immediately echoes with 'let me see' (ἴδω), transferring the verb of seeing between speakers.

elements.context: οἰκίας τε καὶ συσσίτια κοινὰ ἔχοντες

signals.observation: κοινός recurs five times, applied successively to women, children, and then dwellings and meals, expanding the scope of what is held in common.
Three forms of ἀμφισβητέω appear in close succession as Socrates and Glaucon contest which aspects of the proposal will be disputed.

δυνατός recurs across the negotiation; Socrates first isolates it as the remaining question, then proposes to defer it by assuming possibility, and the term returns when he promises later examination.
ὠφέλιμος appears first in the contested pair (beneficial/possible), then in Socrates' hope to escape one horn, and finally in superlative form applied to sacred marriages at the section's close.
Socrates says he hoped to escape (ἀποδράσεσθαι) one argument; Glaucon immediately catches him with the present participle ἀποδιδράσκων.
Socrates asks to 'feast' (ἑορτάσαι) and compares idle thinkers who 'entertain themselves' (ἑστιᾶσθαι), clustering festive/banquet language around the deferral of the feasibility question.
ἀργός intensifies across three forms: the idle (ἀργοί) make an already idle soul (ἀργόν) still idler (ἀργοτέραν).
μεῖξις and μείγνυσθαι appear in sequence: the first names the natural drive toward mixing, the second immediately qualifies that disorderly mixing is impermissible.
Glaucon contrasts geometric necessities with erotic necessities, distinguishing two kinds of ἀνάγκη.
ἐπιτάττω appears in passive and active: auxiliaries willing to do what is commanded, rulers willing to command.

elements.context: ἰδίᾳ δὲ οὐδενὸς οὐδὲν τοιοῦτον κεκτημένου

signals.observation: ἰδίᾳ recurs in both statements of the communal arrangement, each time negated: no private cohabitation, no private possession.

elements.context: εἶεν δʼ ἂν ἱεροὶ οἱ ὠφελιμώτατοι

signals.observation: ἱερός appears twice in immediate succession: marriages are to be made sacred, and the most beneficial ones would be the sacred ones, equating sanctity with benefit.

elements.context: μήτε γονέα ἔκγονον εἰδέναι τὸν αὑτοῦ μήτε παῖδα γονέα

signals.observation: The proposal specifies mutual unknowing: neither parent to know offspring nor child to know parent, a reciprocal epistemic negation.
The τάττω family appears in both positive (διατάττω, arranging) and negative (ἀτάκτως, without order) forms, contrasting ordered regulation with disorderly mixing.
παρίημι appears three times in rapid exchange: Socrates asks twice to be allowed to defer, and Glaucon grants permission with the same verb.
Socrates calls disordered mixing not ὅσιον; Glaucon affirms it is not δίκαιον—two distinct normative terms applied in immediate sequence.

elements.context: ὁρῶ γάρ σου ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ καὶ κύνας θηρευτικοὺς
τὸ τῶν ὀρνίθων καὶ τὸ τῶν κυνῶν γένος

signals.observation: A cluster of animal kinds—hunting dogs, birds, horses, and animals generally—concentrates in the opening exchange as analogues for breeding.

elements.context: τοῖς τούτων γάμοις τε καὶ παιδοποιίᾳ
ἐν τοῖς γάμοις τοίνυν καὶ παιδοποιίαις

signals.observation: γάμος recurs four times, moving from animal matings to human marriage festivals to the number of marriages controlled by rulers.

elements.context: ἐν τοῖς γάμοις τοίνυν καὶ παιδοποιίαις
ῥᾳστώνην … τῆς παιδοποιίας ταῖς τῶν φυλάκων γυναιξίν

signals.observation: παιδοποιία appears first for animals, then for the city's breeding policy, and finally in Glaucon's remark about ease for guardian women.
γενναῖος ('noble/well-bred') and γεννάω ('beget') from the same lexical family appear in close proximity, linking quality of stock to the act of breeding.
Best/worst pairing recurs: ἄριστοι vs. φαυλότατοι for parents, ἀγαθῶν vs. χειρόνων for offspring, sustaining a contrast between superior and inferior throughout.

elements.context: ὅταν δὲ δὴ καὶ φαρμακεύειν δέῃ

signals.observation: A medical cluster—φάρμακον (four times), ἰατρός (twice), φαρμακεύω—concentrates around the analogy between drugs and deception.

elements.context: συχνῷ τῷ ψεύδει καὶ τῇ ἀπάτῃ
ἐν φαρμάκου εἴδει πάντα τὰ τοιαῦτα χρήσιμα

signals.observation: ψεῦδος and ἀπάτη are explicitly equated with φάρμακον: deception is classified as a kind of drug.

elements.context: ταῦτα πάντα γιγνόμενα λανθάνειν πλὴν αὐτοὺς τοὺς ἄρχοντας
ἐν ἀπορρήτῳ τε καὶ ἀδήλῳ κατακρύψουσιν

signals.observation: A cluster of concealment: λανθάνειν, ἀπόρρητος, ἄδηλος, κατακρύπτω, and the provision that no mother recognize her own child.
ἄκρος appears first for the rulers who must be 'top-quality' and then for the flock that must be brought to peak condition.
ποίμνιον ('flock') and ἀγέλη ('herd') apply pastoral-animal vocabulary to the guardian class.

elements.context: κλῆροι δή τινες οἶμαι ποιητέοι κομψοί

signals.observation: A sequence of institutional devices—festivals, sacrifices, hymns, and rigged lots—is laid out as the machinery for concealed eugenic control.

elements.context: κλῆροι δή τινες οἶμαι ποιητέοι κομψοί
αἰτιᾶσθαι ἐφʼ ἑκάστης συνέρξεως τύχην ἀλλὰ μὴ τοὺς ἄρχοντας

signals.observation: The lots are called κομψοί ('clever/elegant'), and their purpose is that the inferior man blame τύχη rather than the rulers—the deception mechanism is made explicit.

elements.context: κοιναὶ μὲν γάρ που καὶ ἀρχαὶ γυναιξί τε καὶ ἀνδράσιν

signals.observation: ἄρχων/ἀρχή recurs densely through the section; rulers are the sole knowing agents of every concealed operation described.

elements.context: ἡ ἀγέλη τῶν φυλάκων ὅτι μάλιστα ἀστασίαστος ἔσται

signals.observation: ἀστασίαστος ('free from faction') names the political goal that concealment of the breeding scheme is meant to secure.

elements.context: ἐξ ἀκμαζόντων δεῖν τὰ ἔκγονα γίγνεσθαι

signals.observation: ἐξ ἀκμαζόντων appears first in the animal-breeding question and returns at the section's close as an established principle for human offspring.

elements.context: τὰς τε μητέρας ἐπὶ τὸν σηκὸν ἄγοντες

elements.form: χωρὶς οἰκούσας ἔν τινι μέρει τῆς πόλεως

signals.observation: The σηκός ('pen/enclosure') is named twice as a separate place within the city where good offspring are taken and mothers are brought, reinforcing the pastoral-spatial arrangement.

elements.context: ὁρῶ γάρ σου ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ καὶ κύνας θηρευτικοὺς

signals.observation: Socrates claims direct observation of Glaucon's household animals and converts it into a question about whether Glaucon has attended to their breeding—seeing leads to asking.

elements.context: πολλὴν ῥᾳστώνην … τῆς παιδοποιίας ταῖς τῶν φυλάκων γυναιξίν

signals.observation: Glaucon calls the arrangement 'great ease' for guardian women; Socrates answers simply πρέπει γάρ ('it is fitting'), a terse endorsement.
A dense cluster of specific numbers defines reproductive age spans for women (20–40) and men (past peak to 55), and the tenth and seventh months define kinship reckoning.
Forms of γεννάω recur densely throughout the section, appearing in varied grammatical forms across the full arc from sanctioned begetting to its cessation and retrospective reckoning.
Sanctioned birth occurs under sacrifices and prayers; unsanctioned birth is contrasted as occurring under darkness with terrible lack of self-control.
Two parallel comparative constructions: from good ones better, from useful ones more useful—each moving from positive to comparative via ἐξ + genitive.

ἅπτω recurs three times: first for transgressive begetting outside age limits, then for unsanctioned union without the ruler's arrangement, then for the sibling prohibition—each a different forbidden touching.

elements.context: νόθον γὰρ καὶ ἀνέγγυον καὶ ἀνίερον

signals.observation: A cluster of sacred/religious language: ὅσιον, priestesses and priests, ἀνίερον (unholy), and the Pythia's sanction for sibling marriage.
Three alpha-privative or negatively marked adjectives in asyndeton characterize the illegitimate child: bastard, unbetrothed, unholy.
A dense enumeration of kinship terms—daughter, mother, son, father, grandparents, siblings—constitutes the system of naming that replaces biological knowledge with temporal convention.
Kinship prohibitions are mapped spatially as upward and downward directions in the generational line.
Darkness (σκότος) characterizes unsanctioned conception; light (φῶς) names what the resulting offspring must not be brought into.

elements.context: αὕτη ἀκμὴ σώματός τε καὶ φρονήσεως

signals.observation: ἀκμή recurs three times: first as a general span, then qualified as the sharpest peak of running, then expanded to encompass both body and intelligence.
The dative τῇ πόλει recurs as the recipient of bearing, begetting, and establishing children; the city itself also appears as subject joining in prayer.

elements.context: πατέρας δὲ καὶ θυγατέρας… πῶς διαγνώσονται ἀλλήλων
ταῦτα πάντα προσερεῖ τὰ μὲν ἄρρενα ὑεῖς

signals.observation: Glaucon asks how fathers and daughters will recognize one another; Socrates answers that recognition is replaced by naming based on temporal convention.
Sibling marriage requires a double authorization: the lot must fall that way and the Pythia must additionally sanction it.
Those past reproductive age are released as 'free' to associate with whom they wish—ἐλεύθερος applied to sexual liberty after state-regulated begetting ends.
The male reproductive start is defined by passing the sharpest peak of running—a physical athletic image (δρόμος, ὀξυτάτη) marking the transition to begetting.

elements.context: ἡ μὲν δὴ κοινωνία… γυναικῶν τε καὶ παίδων

signals.observation: κοινός appears first within the regulatory discussion (begetting 'into the common stock') and returns in the summarizing frame as κοινωνία naming the entire arrangement.

elements.context: τί ποτε τὸ μέγιστον ἀγαθὸν ἔχομεν εἰπεῖν εἰς πόλεως κατασκευήν

signals.observation: μέγιστον ἀγαθόν and μέγιστον κακόν are posed as a paired question, the greatest good and greatest evil for a city.

elements.context: εἰς μὲν τὸ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ ἴχνος ἡμῖν ἁρμόττει

signals.observation: ἁρμόττει and ἀναρμοστεῖ are set against each other as fitting the trace of the good and not fitting that of the bad.

elements.context: εἰς μὲν τὸ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ ἴχνος

signals.observation: The good is spoken of as having an ἴχνος (trace/track) toward which proposals are tested for fit.

elements.context: ὃ ἂν αὐτὴν διασπᾷ καὶ ποιῇ πολλὰς ἀντὶ μιᾶς
τοῦ ὃ ἂν συνδῇ τε καὶ ποιῇ μίαν

signals.observation: διασπᾷ (tearing apart, making many from one) is contrasted with συνδῇ (binding together, making one), with πολλὰς ἀντὶ μιᾶς opposed to μίαν.

elements.context: ἡ μὲν ἡδονῆς τε καὶ λύπης κοινωνία συνδεῖ
ἡ δέ γε τῶν τοιούτων ἰδίωσις διαλύει

signals.observation: κοινωνία (community/sharing) binds while ἰδίωσις (privatization) dissolves; συνδεῖ and διαλύει repeat the binding/loosing contrast.
A dense cluster of pleasure/pain vocabulary: ἡδονή, λύπη, χαίρω, λυπέω, περιαλγής, περιχαρής.

elements.context: τό τε ἐμὸν καὶ τὸ οὐκ ἐμόν

signals.observation: τὸ ἐμόν and τὸ οὐκ ἐμόν are named as utterances (ῥήματα) whose shared or unshared voicing indicates unity or division; ἀλλότριος extends the same axis.

elements.context: ὅταν μὴ ἅμα φθέγγωνται ἐν τῇ πόλει τὰ τοιάδε ῥήματα

signals.observation: Unity is framed as simultaneous utterance (ἅμα φθέγγωνται) of the same words in the city.

elements.context: ὅταν που ἡμῶν δάκτυλός του πληγῇ
πᾶσα ἡ κοινωνία ἡ κατὰ τὸ σῶμα πρὸς τὴν ψυχὴν τεταμένη

signals.observation: The best city is compared to a single human body: when a finger is struck, the whole κοινωνία of body stretched toward soul perceives and co-suffers.

elements.context: πᾶσα ἅμα συνήλγησεν μέρους πονήσαντος ὅλη

signals.observation: Within the body analogy, perception (ᾔσθετο) and shared pain (συνήλγησεν, ἀλγεῖ) cluster together; the whole suffers for the part.
μέρος and ὅλη are set in explicit relation: the whole co-suffers when a part is in pain.
The συν- prefix recurs in συνησθήσεται and συλλυπήσεται, extending the co-suffering/co-rejoicing pattern to the city's relation to each citizen.

elements.context: εἰς μίαν σύνταξιν τὴν τοῦ ἄρχοντος ἐν αὐτῇ

signals.observation: The body's κοινωνία is stretched toward the soul into a single arrangement (σύνταξις) belonging to τοῦ ἄρχοντος—the ruling element within it.

elements.context: ὥρα ἂν εἴη ἐπανιέναι ἡμῖν ἐπὶ τὴν ἡμετέραν πόλιν

signals.observation: The section closes with a proposed return (ἐπανιέναι) to 'our city' to test the argument's agreements there.

elements.context: ἆρʼ οὖν οὐχ ἥδε ἀρχὴ τῆς ὁμολογίας

signals.observation: ὁμολογία opens the section as the starting point of agreement; ὁμολογήματα closes it as what must now be examined—framing the section between two forms of the same root.

elements.context: στοχαζόμενον τὸν νομοθέτην τιθέναι τοὺς νόμους

signals.observation: νομοθέτης near the opening and εὔνομος near the close share the νόμος root.
Three different cities' peoples call their rulers by different names: δεσπότας in most cities, ἄρχοντας in democracies, σωτῆρας καὶ ἐπικούρους in the proposed city.

elements.context: οἱ δʼ ἐν ταῖς ἄλλαις ἄρχοντες τοὺς δήμους

signals.observation: Rulers in other cities call the people δούλους; in the proposed city rulers call the people μισθοδότας τε καὶ τροφέας. The δεσπότας/δούλους pair in other cities contrasts with the reciprocal naming in the proposed city.
Rulers in other cities call each other συνάρχοντας; in the proposed city they call each other συμφύλακας.
The pair οἰκεῖον/ἀλλότριον distinguishes how co-rulers in other cities regard each other; the guardians are said to have no ἀλλότριον among them.
A dense enumeration of kinship terms covers siblings, parents, children, descendants, and ancestors—every guardian encountered is addressed through one of these.

elements.context: τὰς πράξεις πάσας κατὰ τὰ ὀνόματα πράττειν

signals.observation: Socrates poses whether kinship will be ὀνόματα μόνον or accompanied by πράξεις; the question is whether names alone suffice or actions must follow.
ὄνομα/ὀνομάζω recurs across the section, each time in relation to whether naming constitutes or merely accompanies a real relation.

elements.context: τὸ ὅτι τὸ ἐμὸν εὖ πράττει ἢ ὅτι τὸ ἐμὸν κακῶς

signals.observation: τὸ ἐμόν appears as a ῥῆμα citizens will say about shared fortune, then returns as what citizens will ὀνομάζειν in common.

elements.context: ἡ τῶν γυναικῶν τε καὶ παίδων κοινωνία

signals.observation: κοινός/κοινωνία/κοινωνέω appear in high local density at 464a–b, clustered around shared pleasure, pain, and the community of women and children.

elements.context: λύπης τε καὶ ἡδονῆς μάλιστα κοινωνίαν ἕξουσιν
σώματι πρὸς μέρος αὑτοῦ λύπης τε πέρι καὶ ἡδονῆς

signals.observation: The pair λύπη/ἡδονή appears first as what citizens share in common, then in the analogy of city to body.

elements.context: ἀπεικάζοντες εὖ οἰκουμένην πόλιν σώματι πρὸς μέρος αὑτοῦ

signals.observation: The city is compared to a σῶμα in relation to its μέρος regarding pain and pleasure.

elements.context: τοῦ ὑπήκοον δεῖν εἶναι τῶν γονέων

signals.observation: Three dispositions toward parents are named together: αἰδώς, κηδεμονία, and being ὑπήκοος.

elements.context: αὗταί σοι ἢ ἄλλαι φῆμαι ἐξ ἁπάντων τῶν πολιτῶν ὑμνήσουσιν εὐθὺς περὶ τὰ τῶν παίδων ὦτα

signals.observation: φῆμαι are said to be sung (ὑμνήσουσιν) around children's ears—civic speech is figured as something heard by children from all citizens.

elements.context: ἄνευ ἔργων οἰκεῖα ὀνόματα διὰ τῶν στομάτων μόνον φθέγγοιντο

signals.observation: Glaucon calls it γελοῖον to utter kinship names through στόματα alone without ἔργα.

elements.context: οὔτε οἰκίας τούτοις ἰδίας δεῖν εἶναι

signals.observation: οἰκεῖος appears twice describing kinship names, then οἰκία appears at 464b as private houses the guardians must not have—the lexical family spans kinship-belonging and household-property.
ἐπίκουρος first appears as what the people call the rulers, then returns as the group for whom the κοινωνία of women and children is the cause of the greatest good.

elements.context: μηδὲν ἴδιον ἐκτῆσθαι πλὴν τὸ σῶμα
χρημάτων ἢ παίδων καὶ συγγενῶν κτῆσιν

signals.observation: Forms of κτάομαι/κτῆσις recur across the section: κτῆμα (what guardians lack), κτήσασθαι (private acquisition dragged home), ἐκτῆσθαι (nothing private possessed except the body), κτῆσιν (possession as cause of faction).

elements.context: ὁ φύλαξ ἐπιχειρήσει εὐδαίμων γίγνεσθαι, ὥστε μηδὲ φύλαξ εἶναι

signals.observation: φύλαξ recurs throughout; at 466b it appears twice in a single clause where being a guardian and ceasing to be one are juxtaposed.

elements.context: μηδὲν ἴδιον ἐκτῆσθαι πλὴν τὸ σῶμα
πάντα πάντῃ κατὰ τὸ δυνατὸν κοινωνεῖν

signals.observation: ἴδιος and κοινός/κοινωνία are set against each other repeatedly: private possession is what tears the city apart, common holding is what unifies it. κοινωνεῖν closes the section.

elements.context: ἧττον ἐπὶ μείζους ἂν ἴοι στάσεις
τούτων μὴν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς μὴ στασιαζόντων
ἡ ἄλλη πόλις πρὸς τούτους ἢ πρὸς ἀλλήλους διχοστατήσῃ

signals.observation: στάσις/στασιάζω recurs with the alpha-privative ἀστασίαστος and the compound διχοστατέω, forming a cluster around faction and its absence.

elements.context: τὸ ἐμὸν ὀνομάζοντας μὴ τὸ αὐτὸ ἀλλʼ ἄλλον ἄλλο

signals.observation: τὸ ἐμόν names the act of calling things 'mine'; the phrase ἄλλον ἄλλο immediately specifies the divergence this produces—each person calling a different thing his own.
Pleasure and pain appear twice in close proximity: first as private (ἡδονάς τε καὶ ἀλγηδόνας … ἰδίας), then as shared (ὁμοπαθεῖς λύπης τε καὶ ἡδονῆς), with the shift from ἰδίας to ὁμοπαθεῖς.

elements.context: μηδὲν ἴδιον ἐκτῆσθαι πλὴν τὸ σῶμα

signals.observation: The body is the sole private possession (πλὴν τὸ σῶμα) and then returns as the domain where physical self-defence is justified (σωμάτων ἐπιμελείᾳ).
A cluster of kinship terms—parents, sons, brothers, fathers—appears as the basis for the restraining force (αἰδώς and δέος) that prevents violence among guardians.

elements.context: ἱκανὼ γὰρ τὼ φύλακε κωλύοντε, δέος τε καὶ αἰδώς

signals.observation: δέος and αἰδώς are presented as a dual pair (τὼ φύλακε) guarding conduct: αἰδώς restrains touching parents, δέος concerns others coming to aid.

elements.context: πρεσβυτέρῳ μὴν νεωτέρων πάντων ἄρχειν τε καὶ κολάζειν
νεώτερος πρεσβύτερον … οὔτε ἄλλο βιάζεσθαι ἐπιχειρήσει

signals.observation: πρεσβύτερος and νεώτερος are explicitly contrasted: the elder commands and punishes, the younger does not use force against the elder.

elements.context: διὰ σμικρόν που μέρος εὐδαιμονίζονται ἐκεῖνοι

signals.observation: εὐδαίμων and cognates recur densely: the guardians were said not to be made happy, the city is to be made happiest, the guardian who pursues private happiness ceases to be a guardian.

elements.context: τοῦ μακαριστοῦ βίου ὃν οἱ Ὀλυμπιονῖκαι ζῶσι μακαριώτερον
τοῦ γε τῶν Ὀλυμπιονικῶν πολύ τε καλλίων

signals.observation: The Olympian victors serve as a comparative measure: guardians live more blessedly than they, and the guardians' victory (σωτηρία of the whole city) is called καλλίων.

elements.context: ἥ τε γὰρ τῶνδε νίκη καλλίων
νίκην τε γὰρ νικῶσι συμπάσης τῆς πόλεως σωτηρίαν

signals.observation: νίκη and νικάω appear together; the guardians' victory is specified as the salvation (σωτηρίαν) of the entire city.

elements.context: ἡ τʼ ἐκ τοῦ δημοσίου τροφὴ τελεωτέρα
τροφῇ τε καὶ τοῖς ἄλλοις πᾶσιν

signals.observation: τροφή recurs: guardians receive sustenance from others (464c), ordinary people suffer over household maintenance (465c), and the guardians' public maintenance is called τελεωτέρα (465d).
ἀπαλλάσσω recurs three times, each time marking a riddance: from lawsuits, from petty evils, and from all such things together.

elements.context: γνώσεται τὸν Ἡσίοδον ὅτι τῷ ὄντι ἦν σοφὸς

signals.observation: Hesiod is cited by name; the quoted maxim (the half is more than the whole, WD 40) is applied to the guardian who would seize everything in the city.
Women guardians are compared to dogs (κύνας) in the context of co-guarding and co-hunting.

elements.context: τὴν τοῦ θήλεος πρὸς τὸ ἄρρεν

signals.observation: θῆλυς and ἄρρην are paired at the section's close, with the dual πεφύκατον πρὸς ἀλλήλω κοινωνεῖν asserting their natural partnership.

elements.context: θέμενοι παρὰ γυναῖκάς τε καὶ οἰκέτας

signals.observation: A rapid sequence of participles describes the ordinary person's financial struggles: borrowing, denying debts, procuring by any means, depositing with wives and servants, handing over stewardship.
The proverbial phrase δῆλα καὶ τυφλῷ ('obvious even to a blind man') is the interlocutor's response to the catalogue of petty evils.

elements.context: τοῦτο μέν, εἴ που παραπίπτοι, εἰς αὖθις σκεψοίμεθα

elements.form: νῦν ἡμῖν ὁ τῶν ἐπικούρων βίος
elements.context: τοῦ γε τῶν Ὀλυμπιονικῶν πολύ τε καλλίων καὶ ἀμείνων φαίνεται

signals.observation: An earlier deferral (we said we would examine the guardians' happiness later) is recalled (μέμνησαι) and answered within this section by the claim that the auxiliaries' life now appears far finer than the Olympic victors'.

elements.context: πανταχῇ δὴ ἐκ τῶν νόμων εἰρήνην πρὸς ἀλλήλους

signals.observation: διασπᾶν names the tearing apart of the city early in the section; εἰρήνην names the peace achieved among the men later, marking opposite poles of civic condition.

elements.context: ὥσπερ οἱ τῶν ἄλλων δημιουργῶν θεῶνται ταῦτα
ἐμπειρίᾳ τε καὶ θέᾳ τῶν προσηκόντων
ἄξιον κινδύνου θεωρεῖν ἢ μὴ τὰ περὶ τὸν πόλεμον
ἐφʼ ἵππων ἀκτέον ἐπὶ τὴν θέαν
κάλλιστά τε θεάσονται τὸ αὑτῶν ἔργον

signals.observation: Forms of θεάομαι, θεωρέω, θέα, and θεωρός recur densely throughout the section, constituting the central lexical family for the children's relation to war.

elements.context: δημιουργόν τινα δεῖ καθιστάναι ἢ γεωργόν

signals.observation: δημιουργός/δημιουργέω appears first as the craftsman analogy for children learning by watching, then returns as the demotion punishment for cowardly soldiers.

elements.context: ὥσπερ οἱ τῶν ἄλλων δημιουργῶν θεῶνται

signals.observation: δημιουργός first names the craftsman whose children watch and learn; it returns as the status to which a cowardly guardian is demoted.

elements.context: κίνδυνος δέ, ὦ Σώκρατες, οὐ σμικρὸς

signals.observation: κίνδυνος and related forms cluster densely in the exchange about whether children should be exposed to war.

elements.context: πρὸς δὲ τῇ θέᾳ διακονεῖν καὶ ὑπηρετεῖν
διακονεῖν καὶ ὑπηρετεῖν πάντα τὰ περὶ τὸν πόλεμον

signals.observation: A cluster of service-words (διακονεῖν, ὑπηρετεῖν, θεραπεύειν) describes the children's role alongside watching.
The metaphor of 'winging' children so they can 'fly away' is then literalized as mounting them on horses.

elements.context: ἐπὶ τοὺς ἵππους ἀναβιβαστέον ὡς νεωτάτους

signals.observation: The figurative proposal to 'wing' the children is immediately answered by the concrete prescription to mount them on horses.

elements.context: ἄξουσι τῶν παίδων εἰς τὸν πόλεμον

signals.observation: Terms for the children's age and maturity (ἁδροί, παῖδας, παιδία, νεωτάτους, τελεωθέντας) recur throughout, marking stages of readiness.
A concise contrast: into some campaigns they will lead the children, from others they will hold back.
The potter analogy is specified: potters' children serve and watch for a long time before touching the craft, offered as a parallel to guardians' children watching war.
ζῷον appears first in the question whether the community is possible as in other animals, then returns in the claim that every animal fights better in the presence of its offspring.
The horses' qualities are specified by contrast: not spirited or combative, but swift and easy to rein—qualities selected for escape rather than battle.

elements.context: τὸν λιπόντα τάξιν ἢ ὅπλα ἀποβαλόντα
τὸν δὲ ζῶντα εἰς τοὺς πολεμίους ἁλόντα

signals.observation: Two cases of military failure are distinguished: desertion/cowardice and capture alive, each receiving a different prescribed consequence.

elements.context: ἆρʼ οὐ δωρεὰν διδόναι τοῖς ἑλοῦσι
χρῆσθαι τῇ ἄγρᾳ ὅτι ἂν βούλωνται

signals.observation: The captured soldier is described as a 'gift' (δωρεάν) and a 'catch' (ἄγρα), applying hunting/gift language to the fate of the prisoner.
A sequence of verbal adjectives in -τέον marks prescriptive necessities across the passage.
Three honors are proposed in ascending sequence: crowning, clasping hands, kissing. Each is an aorist passive infinitive, and the third is presented as the most controversial.

elements.context: τὸν δὲ ἀριστεύσαντά τε καὶ εὐδοκιμήσαντα

signals.observation: εὐδοκιμέω recurs three times: first for the living warrior, then in the Homeric example, then for the warrior who dies—shifting from life honors to posthumous status.

elements.context: τοὺς ἀγαθούς, καθʼ ὅσον ἂν ἀγαθοὶ φαίνωνται

elements.form: τοὺς ἀγαθοὺς ἄνδρας τε καὶ γυναῖκας

signals.observation: ἀγαθός recurs densely across the section, applied to the living (marriages, feasting) and finally to those judged good in life who have died.

elements.context: ἅμα τῷ τιμᾶσθαι καὶ τὴν ἰσχὺν αὐξήσει

signals.observation: τιμάω/τιμή forms cluster densely, linking Homeric precedent to the city's own practice of honoring.
πεισόμεθα appears three times: first obeying Homer, then introduced with negation regarding Hesiod, then affirmed—the negation is rhetorical and immediately reversed.

elements.context: ἐπειδάν τινες τοῦ τοιούτου γένους τελευτήσωσιν
ὅταν τις γήρᾳ ἤ τινι ἄλλῳ τρόπῳ τελευτήσῃ

signals.observation: τελευτάω recurs three times as the section shifts from living honors to posthumous honors, marking each mention of death.
A cluster of concrete honor-items: sacrifices, hymns, seats, meat, cups—combining civic ritual with Homeric feasting vocabulary.
The fallen brave are assigned to the golden race, invoking Hesiodic genealogy of races.
The Hesiodic quotation names the dead as holy daimones, averters of evil, and guardians of mortals—φύλακες applied to the heroic dead.
φύλακες appears in the Hesiodic citation describing the golden-race dead as guardians of humans.

elements.context: τοὺς δαιμονίους τε καὶ θείους τιθέναι

signals.observation: The dead become δαιμόνιοι καὶ θεῖοι; their tombs (θήκας) will receive ongoing cult: θεραπεύσομεν and προσκυνήσομεν.

elements.context: τῶν δὲ δὴ ἀποθανόντων ἐπὶ στρατιᾶς

signals.observation: ἐπὶ στρατιᾶς frames both the living warrior's honors and the dead warrior's honors, marking the transition between the two.

elements.context: μηδενὶ ἐξεῖναι ἀπαρνηθῆναι ὃν ἂν βούληται φιλεῖν

signals.observation: φιλέω moves from active-and-passive infinitive pair (kissing and being kissed) to a law that no one may refuse to kiss whomever the brave warrior wishes.
Homer is cited as authority three times for living honors; Hesiod is then introduced with apparent negation for posthumous honors, but the negation is immediately reversed into affirmation.

elements.context: ἐάν τίς του τύχῃ ἐρῶν ἢ ἄρρενος ἢ θηλείας

signals.observation: Erotic desire (ἐρῶν) for male or female is linked to battlefield incentive; marriages (γάμοι) for the brave are recalled as already established.

elements.context: τῶν δὲ δὴ ἀποθανόντων ἐπὶ στρατιᾶς

elements.form: γήρᾳ ἤ τινι ἄλλῳ τρόπῳ τελευτήσῃ

signals.observation: Posthumous honors initially apply to those who die on campaign; they are then extended to those who die of old age or otherwise, provided they are judged outstandingly good.

elements.context: ἐπὶ δὲ τῇ τοῦ ἀλλοτρίου πόλεμος
ἐπὶ μὲν οὖν τῇ τοῦ οἰκείου ἔχθρᾳ στάσις κέκληται
νοσεῖν δʼ ἐν τῷ τοιούτῳ τὴν Ἑλλάδα καὶ στασιάζειν

signals.observation: πόλεμος and στάσις are explicitly distinguished as two names for two kinds of enmity, one applying to ἀλλότριον, the other to οἰκεῖον; their cognates recur throughout the passage in application to these categories.
Two paired oppositions—οἰκεῖον/συγγενές vs. ἀλλότριον/ὀθνεῖον—are set out as the basis for the πόλεμος/στάσις distinction.

elements.context: τῷ δὲ βαρβαρικῷ ὀθνεῖόν τε καὶ ἀλλότριον

signals.observation: Ἕλλην/Ἑλληνικός and βάρβαρος/βαρβαρικός recur densely throughout as the governing contrast for all the specific prohibitions.
Enslavement vocabulary clusters at the opening and returns near the close; the prohibition against enslaving Greeks is framed partly by fear of barbarian enslavement.
Stripping the dead is named three times in sequence with escalating moral characterization: first as a question, then as ἀνελεύθερον and φιλοχρήματον, then as something to be abandoned.
The coward's choice is presented as turning toward the dead (τεθνεῶτα) instead of going toward the one still fighting (μαχόμενον).

elements.context: τὸ σῶμα τοῦ τεθνεῶτος ἀποπταμένου τοῦ ἐχθροῦ

signals.observation: The enemy is said to have 'flown away' (ἀποπταμένου) from the body, leaving behind 'that with which he fought'—the body is explicitly distinguished from the enemy.

elements.context: τῶν κυνῶν αἳ τοῖς λίθοις οἷς ἂν βληθῶσι χαλεπαίνουσι

signals.observation: Those who strip corpses are compared to dogs that rage at the stones thrown at them while not touching the thrower—an explicit analogy for misdirected hostility.
Land-ravaging and house-burning recur as a paired action four times, with variation between τέμνω and κείρω for ravaging and between ἐμπίμπρημι and ἀνατρέπω for destruction of houses.

elements.context: τὴν τροφόν τε καὶ μητέρα κείρειν

signals.observation: The land is called 'nurse and mother' (τροφόν τε καὶ μητέρα) in the context of why ravaging it in stasis is intolerable.

elements.context: νοσεῖν δʼ ἐν τῷ τοιούτῳ τὴν Ἑλλάδα

signals.observation: Greek-on-Greek conflict is called νοσεῖν (being sick), and the proper response is σωφρονίζειν (bringing to their senses)—correction rather than destruction—with σωφρονισταί explicitly opposed to πολέμιοι.

elements.context: διανοεῖσθαι ὡς διαλλαγησομένων καὶ οὐκ ἀεὶ πολεμησόντων

signals.observation: The expectation of future reconciliation (διαλλαγησομένων) is stated as a general principle and then applied specifically to the guardians' city.

elements.context: πολὺ γάρ … ἡμερωτέρων αὕτη ἡ διάνοια

signals.observation: ἥμερος appears first as a comparative characterizing the gentler disposition, then in the positive describing the guardians' city—linking the policy to the character of its citizens.

elements.context: μή τι μίασμα ᾖ πρὸς ἱερὸν τὰ τοιαῦτα ἀπὸ τῶν οἰκείων φέρειν
ἐὰν μή τι δὴ ὁ θεὸς ἄλλο λέγῃ

signals.observation: Bringing arms of fellow Greeks to temples is called a potential μίασμα (pollution), with a reservation for divine exception (ἐὰν μή τι ὁ θεὸς ἄλλο λέγῃ).

elements.form: ὀλίγους ἀεὶ ἐχθροὺς τοὺς αἰτίους τῆς διαφορᾶς
πάντας ἐχθροὺς αὑτοῖς εἶναι, καὶ ἄνδρας καὶ γυναῖκας καὶ παῖδας

signals.observation: A contrast between treating everyone in a city as enemies (men, women, children) and recognizing only the few responsible (ὀλίγους … τοὺς αἰτίους) as enemies.

elements.form: οἱ αἴτιοι ἀναγκασθῶσιν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀναιτίων ἀλγούντων δοῦναι δίκην

signals.observation: The limit of the conflict is set at the point where the guilty (αἴτιοι) are compelled by the suffering of the innocent (ἀναιτίων ἀλγούντων) to give justice (δοῦναι δίκην).

elements.context: ὅλῳ καὶ παντί … διαφέρει τὸ φείδεσθαι

signals.observation: φείδεσθαι (sparing) is proposed and immediately emphatically endorsed with ὅλῳ καὶ παντί.
Stripping corpses receives a concentrated cluster of moral epithets: ἀνελεύθερον, φιλοχρήματον, and γυναικείας τε καὶ σμικρᾶς διανοίας.
φύσει is used in immediate succession for opposite relations: Greeks and barbarians are enemies φύσει, while Greeks among themselves are friends φύσει.

elements.context: τὸ ὡς δυνατὴ αὕτη ἡ πολιτεία γενέσθαι καὶ τίνα τρόπον ποτὲ δυνατή
ὡς καὶ δυνατὸν γενέσθαι τοιοῦτον ἄνδρα
πῇ μάλιστα καὶ κατὰ τί δυνατώτατʼ ἂν εἴη
οὐ μέντοι σμικροῦ γε οὐδὲ ῥᾳδίου, δυνατοῦ δέ

signals.observation: Forms of δυνατός recur densely throughout the section, first as Glaucon's demand, then in Socrates' reframing of what demonstration of possibility requires.

elements.context: γράψας παράδειγμα οἷον ἂν εἴη ὁ κάλλιστος ἄνθρωπος

signals.observation: παράδειγμα appears three times: for the inquiry into justice, for the painter's model of the most beautiful human, and for the city constructed in speech.

elements.context: τὸ μέγιστον καὶ χαλεπώτατον τῆς τρικυμίας

signals.observation: A wave cluster: two waves already escaped, the third and greatest now approaching, with κατακλύσειν adding flooding/inundation.

elements.context: ἀγαπήσομεν ἐὰν ὅτι ἐγγύτατα αὐτῆς ᾖ

signals.observation: ἀγαπάω recurs: first about being satisfied with proximity to justice itself, then about being satisfied with finding approximate possibility—Socrates applies the same verb of contentment to the new question.

elements.context: τοιαῦτα παντάπασι καὶ τῷ ἔργῳ δεῖν γιγνόμενα
φύσιν ἔχει πρᾶξιν λέξεως ἧττον ἀληθείας ἐφάπτεσθαι

signals.observation: A contrast between λόγος/λέξις and ἔργον/πρᾶξις is articulated: speech and deed differ in their relation to truth, and Socrates insists the city was made in λόγῳ, not required to match exactly in ἔργῳ.

elements.context: ὡς ἂν ἐγγύτατα τῶν εἰρημένων πόλις οἰκήσειεν

signals.observation: ἐγγύτατα appears first for the just man's proximity to justice itself, then for the city's proximity to what was described in speech.

elements.context: πάντα εἰς τὸ γράμμα ἱκανῶς ἀποδούς
οἷον ἂν εἴη ὁ κάλλιστος ἄνθρωπος

signals.observation: A painter analogy cluster: ζωγράφος, γράψας, γράμμα, and κάλλιστος ἄνθρωπος appear together as Socrates compares the model city to a painting of the most beautiful human.

elements.context: εἰ γένοιτο, πάντʼ ἂν εἴη ἀγαθὰ πόλει ᾗ γένοιτο
εἴ ποτέ τις ἀνάγκη βοηθείας γένοιτο
πῇ δυνατὴ γίγνεσθαι αὕτη ἡ πολιτεία

signals.observation: Forms of γίγνομαι recur densely, mostly in optative (γένοιτο) for hypothetical coming-into-being, paired repeatedly with δυνατός.
A numerical sequence—one, if not two, if not the fewest—specifying the smallest change needed, resolved immediately to ἑνός at 473c.

elements.context: οἱ βασιλῆς τε νῦν λεγόμενοι καὶ δυνάσται φιλοσοφήσωσι
τοῦτο εἰς ταὐτὸν συμπέσῃ, δύναμίς τε πολιτικὴ καὶ φιλοσοφία
τῶν δὲ νῦν πορευομένων χωρὶς ἐφʼ ἑκάτερον
αἱ πολλαὶ φύσεις ἐξ ἀνάγκης ἀποκλεισθῶσιν

signals.observation: The philosopher-king statement is structured as a contrast between currently separate (χωρίς, ἐφʼ ἑκάτερον) paths that must fall together (εἰς ταὐτὸν συμπέσῃ), with those going separately shut out (ἀποκλεισθῶσιν).

elements.context: εἰκότως ἄρα ὤκνουν τε καὶ ἐδεδοίκη

signals.observation: Hesitation and fear cluster: ὀκνέω and δείδω appear together at 472a, and ὄκνος returns at 473e after the philosopher-king statement has been made.

elements.context: μέλλει γέλωτί τε ἀτεχνῶς ὥσπερ κῦμα ἐκγελῶν

signals.observation: Ridicule and disrepute cluster: γέλως, ἐκγελάω, ἀδοξία, and τωθάζω gather around the anticipated response to the philosopher-king proposal.

elements.context: φυῇ τε εἰς τὸ δυνατὸν καὶ φῶς ἡλίου ἴδῃ

signals.observation: The politeia is said to need to grow (φυῇ) into the possible and see the light of the sun—a conjunction of natural growth and sunlight applied to the constitution's realization.
Glaucon depicts opponents stripping off cloaks, seizing weapons, and running at full stretch—a vivid military attack image applied to intellectual opponents.

elements.context: εἰ μὴ ἀμυνῇ τῷ λόγῳ καὶ ἐκφεύξῃ

signals.observation: ἀμύνω appears first as what Socrates must do with λόγος, then as what Glaucon promises to do for him; Glaucon names himself βοηθός.

elements.context: ὃς ἂν ἐκείνοις ὅτι ὁμοιότατος ᾖ

signals.observation: ὁμοιότατος and ὁμοιοτάτην appear in immediate proximity: the person most like the paradigm will have the most similar portion.

elements.context: οὐ μέντοι σμικροῦ γε οὐδὲ ῥᾳδίου

signals.observation: σμικρός recurs: the smallest change is sought (σμικροτάτου, σμικροτάτων), then Socrates concedes the one change is not small (οὐ σμικροῦ).
παραλείπω appears twice: Glaucon says he will supply what Socrates leaves out, then notes goods left out at home.

elements.context: εἰ δὲ καὶ τὸ θῆλυ συστρατεύοιτο

signals.observation: Kinship terms—brothers, fathers, sons—cluster as names soldiers call each other, followed immediately by the female element joining the campaign.
A dense concentration of φιλο- compounds accumulates across the section, each naming a different object of desire: boys, wine, honor, learning, food, wisdom, spectacles, listening, craft.
Forms of πᾶς recur with high density, each time insisting on totality of the relevant object—the lover must embrace all of whatever is loved.

elements.form: τὸ μὲν φιλοῦντα ἐκείνου, τὸ δὲ μή

signals.observation: A μέν … δέ structure expressing partial desire (loving some but not all) recurs and is each time denied.

elements.context: ἅπτεσθαί τε φιλοσοφίας ἡγεμονεύειν τʼ ἐν πόλει

elements.form: μήτε ἅπτεσθαι ἀκολουθεῖν τε τῷ ἡγουμένῳ

signals.observation: ἅπτεσθαι and ἡγεμονεύειν/ἀκολουθεῖν are distributed in a contrast: some are to touch philosophy and lead, others are not to touch it and must follow.
ἐπιθυμ- forms move from honor-lovers to a general principle about desiring the whole of a kind, then to food as analogy.
A catalogue of physical features—snub nose, hooked nose, in-between, dark, pale, honey-colored—illustrates how the lover renames every appearance to make it attractive.
ἐρωτικός/ἐραστής forms cluster around the lover analogy, with Glaucon addressed as ἀνδρὶ ἐρωτικῷ and the term then applied to the class of lovers generally.

elements.context: τὸν δὲ δὴ εὐχερῶς ἐθέλοντα παντὸς μαθήματος γεύεσθαι

signals.observation: δυσχερ- (difficulty/disgust) and εὐχερῶς (ease/readiness) appear as a contrasting pair; εὐχερῶς first describes the lover's easy tolerance of pallor, then returns to describe the philosopher's willing tasting of every learning.
A food/appetite vocabulary—tasting, hunger, insatiability, food-loving vs. food-averse—is applied to learning in a sustained analogy.
φιλοθεάμονες first names spectacle-lovers whom Glaucon would awkwardly class as philosophers; Socrates then reclaims the term for true philosophers as τῆς ἀληθείας φιλοθεάμονας.

elements.context: ὥσπερ δὲ ἀπομεμισθωκότες τὰ ὦτα ἐπακοῦσαι πάντων χορῶν

signals.observation: Glaucon describes the φιλήκοοι as having 'hired out their ears' and running around at the Dionysia to hear every chorus, a concrete image of indiscriminate sensory pursuit.
ἕκαστον appears in two parallel clauses: each form is one in itself, yet each appears many through participation in actions, bodies, and mutual association.
ἀκολουθέω appears first as the role assigned to non-philosophers (following the leader in the city), then immediately as Socrates' imperative to Glaucon to follow his argument.
ἡγεμονεύειν and ἡγουμένῳ from the same root appear in close succession, the first naming the philosopher's political role, the second naming the person others follow.

elements.context: ἀναμιμνῄσκειν οὖν σε … δεήσει, ἢ μέμνησαι

signals.observation: Socrates asks whether reminding will be necessary or Glaucon remembers; Glaucon immediately concedes that reminding is indeed necessary, completing the proposed action.
The section moves from the need to define/distinguish (διορίσασθαι, ὁρίζεσθαι) to the act of dividing (διαιρῶ) at its close.
Paired comparatives set greater/more dignified against smaller/more trivial in describing the honor-lovers' willingness to accept any source of honor.
Three pairings of opposites—beautiful/ugly, just/unjust, good/bad—are listed as instances of each form being one yet appearing many.
Two compound φιλο- adjectives name the lovers of sights and sounds as a pair.
Three concrete sensible particulars—voices, colors, shapes—are listed as objects the sight-lovers embrace.

elements.context: τὴν φύσιν ἰδεῖν τε καὶ ἀσπάσασθαι

signals.observation: ἀσπάζομαι appears first for the sight-lovers embracing beautiful particulars, then for their inability to embrace the nature of the beautiful itself.

elements.context: ἐπʼ αὐτὸ τὸ καλὸν δυνατοὶ ἰέναι

signals.observation: ἀδύνατος describes the sight-lovers' thought; δυνατοί describes those able to approach the beautiful itself.

elements.context: ὄναρ ἢ ὕπαρ δοκεῖ σοι ζῆν

signals.observation: The dreaming/waking pair is posed as a question for the opinion-holder, then answered as ὕπαρ for the one who sees the beautiful itself.

elements.context: τὸ ὀνειρώττειν ἆρα οὐ τόδε ἐστίν

signals.observation: ὀνειρώττειν is defined and then immediately applied to the person who mistakes likenesses for originals.

elements.context: τὸ ὅμοιόν τῳ μὴ ὅμοιον ἀλλʼ αὐτὸ ἡγῆται εἶναι ᾧ ἔοικεν

signals.observation: The definition of dreaming turns on taking the likeness (ὅμοιον) for the thing itself (αὐτό) it resembles.

elements.context: οὔτε τὰ μετέχοντα αὐτὸ οὔτε αὐτὸ τὰ μετέχοντα

signals.observation: μετέχοντα appears three times in close succession describing the participatory relation and the waking person's ability to distinguish participants from the thing itself.
γνώμη and δόξα are assigned to the two types: the knower's thought is γνώμη, the opiner's is δόξα.

elements.context: ὁ γιγνώσκων γιγνώσκει τὶ ἢ οὐδέν

signals.observation: Forms of γιγνώσκω recur densely from 476d through 477a as the argument moves from naming the knower to establishing that the fully real is fully knowable.

elements.context: ἕξομέν τι παραμυθεῖσθαι αὐτὸν καὶ πείθειν ἠρέμα

signals.observation: The proposed approach to the opinion-holder combines soothing (παραμυθεῖσθαι), gentle persuading (πείθειν ἠρέμα), and concealing (ἐπικρυπτόμενοι) that he is not healthy (οὐχ ὑγιαίνει).
οἶδα appears twice in the conciliatory address, framing the approach as welcoming anyone who knows something.

elements.context: τὸ μὲν παντελῶς ὂν παντελῶς γνωστόν
μὴ ὂν δὲ μηδαμῇ πάντῃ ἄγνωστον

signals.observation: The section concludes by correlating degrees of being with degrees of knowability: παντελῶς ὄν with παντελῶς γνωστόν, μὴ ὄν with πάντῃ ἄγνωστον.
γνωστόν and ἄγνωστον stand as opposites at the section's close, each qualified by a totalizing adverb.

elements.context: αὐτοῦ δὲ τοῦ καλοῦ ἀδύνατος αὐτῶν ἡ διάνοια
τούτου μὲν τὴν διάνοιαν ὡς γιγνώσκοντος

signals.observation: διάνοια first names the thought that cannot reach the beautiful itself, then names the thought of the one who does know—applied to contrasting figures.

elements.context: πάντα τὰ ἐκ τῶν τοιούτων δημιουργούμενα

signals.observation: δημιουργούμενα names the crafted products made from beautiful voices, colors, and shapes—the objects the sight-lovers embrace.
Those able to approach the beautiful itself are called σπάνιοι—rare.

elements.context: ἐπὶ δὲ τῷ μεταξὺ τούτῳ μεταξύ τι καὶ ζητητέον
μεταξὺ ἄρα ἂν εἴη τούτοιν δόξα
τὸ μεταξὺ αὖ φανὲν ἀγνοίας καὶ ἐπιστήμης

signals.observation: μεταξύ recurs densely throughout, framing the section's spatial placement of δόξα between knowledge and ignorance, appearing at both the opening hypothesis and the closing conclusion.

elements.context: ἄλλην δύναμιν ἐπιστήμης ἢ τὴν αὐτήν
φήσομεν δυνάμεις εἶναι γένος τι τῶν ὄντων
αἷς δὴ καὶ ἡμεῖς δυνάμεθα ἃ δυνάμεθα
δυνάμεως γὰρ ἐγὼ οὔτε τινὰ χρόαν ὁρῶ

signals.observation: The δύναμις word-family recurs with high density, including the verb δύναμαι doubled in the same clause (δυνάμεθα ἃ δυνάμεθα), establishing the criterion by which ἐπιστήμη and δόξα are distinguished.

elements.context: μὴ ὄντι μὴν ἄγνοιαν ἐξ ἀνάγκης ἀπέδομεν

signals.observation: Three terms—ἐπιστήμη, δόξα, ἄγνοια—are repeatedly set in contrast and arranged in a triadic structure throughout the section.
Sight and hearing are named as examples of δυνάμεις, while color and shape are named as perceptible features that δύναμις lacks—a cluster of sensory and visible-form terms.
ἀναμάρτητον and μὴ ἀναμαρτήτῳ are set in immediate contrast, distinguishing ἐπιστήμη (unerring) from δόξα (not unerring).

elements.context: γνώσεως μέν σοι φαίνεται δόξα σκοτωδέστερον

signals.observation: δόξα is characterized as darker than knowledge and brighter than ignorance—a light/dark contrast pair.
σαφήνεια and ἀσάφεια are paired as the two directions in which δόξα might exceed its boundaries, both denied.

elements.context: ἐπὶ μὲν τῷ ὄντι γνῶσις ἦν
ἔσται γνωστόν τε καὶ δοξαστὸν τὸ αὐτό

signals.observation: The γιγνώσκω/γνῶσις family recurs across noun, infinitive, finite verb, and verbal adjective forms, consistently linked to τὸ ὄν.

elements.context: ἆρʼ οὖν τὸ μὴ ὂν δοξάζει
γνωστόν τε καὶ δοξαστὸν τὸ αὐτό

signals.observation: δόξα/δοξάζω/δοξαστόν recur across noun, verb, and verbal adjective, paralleling the γνῶσις family.

elements.context: γνωστόν τε καὶ δοξαστὸν τὸ αὐτό

signals.observation: The verbal adjectives γνωστόν and δοξαστόν are placed in direct syntactic parallel, forming a pair that is then denied identity.

elements.context: ἐπιστήμη μὲν ἐπὶ τῷ ὄντι πέφυκε

signals.observation: πέφυκε recurs to express the natural assignment of each δύναμις; πέφανται closes the section with a perfect of appearing rather than natural assignment.
Spatial placement language—lying between, being stationed upon, inside, outside—locates δόξα positionally relative to knowledge and ignorance.

elements.context: τοῦ εἰλικρινῶς ὄντος καὶ τοῦ αὖ μηδαμῇ ὄντος
μεταξὺ κεῖσθαι τοῦ εἰλικρινῶς ὄντος τε καὶ τοῦ πάντως μὴ ὄντος

signals.observation: The phrase εἰλικρινῶς ὄντος appears at 477a and returns at 478d in the recapitulation, while its opposite shifts from μηδαμῇ ὄντος to πάντως μὴ ὄντος.

elements.context: νῦν δέ γε πέφανται μεταξὺ τούτοιν ὃ δὴ καλοῦμεν δόξαν

signals.observation: The section opens with ζητητέον (something must be sought between ignorance and knowledge) and closes with πέφανται (it has now appeared), completing the search.

elements.context: δυνάμεως γὰρ ἐγὼ οὔτε τινὰ χρόαν ὁρῶ

signals.observation: Three verbs of seeing cluster in the account of δύναμις: ὁρῶ (what one cannot see of a power), ἀποβλέπων (looking toward visible features of other things), βλέπω (looking only at what a power is set over).

elements.context: ἐφʼ ᾧ τε ἔστι καὶ ὃ ἀπεργάζεται
τὸ αὐτὸ ἀπεργαζομένην τὴν αὐτὴν καλῶ
ἐπὶ ἑτέρῳ καὶ ἕτερον ἀπεργαζομένην ἄλλην

signals.observation: ἀπεργάζομαι recurs three times in the criterion for distinguishing δυνάμεις: what a power accomplishes is one of two identifying marks.
ἐπιστήμη is called the strongest (ἐρρωμενεστάτην) of all δυνάμεις—a superlative that singles it out within the class just defined.

elements.form: τοῦ εἶναί τε καὶ μὴ εἶναι
elements.context: τὸ ἀμφοτέρων μετέχον, τοῦ εἶναί τε καὶ μὴ εἶναι

elements.form: οὐσίας τε καὶ τοῦ μὴ εἶναι
elements.context: μεταξὺ οὐσίας τε καὶ τοῦ μὴ εἶναι

signals.observation: The pairing of being and not-being recurs across the section in varied formulations: participation in both, neither stably, and a midpoint between οὐσία and μὴ εἶναι.

elements.context: τοῖς δὲ μεταξὺ τὰ μεταξὺ ἀποδιδόντες
μεταξὺ οὐσίας τε καὶ τοῦ μὴ εἶναι
τῇ μεταξὺ δυνάμει τὸ μεταξὺ πλανητὸν

signals.observation: μεταξύ recurs densely, applied to the objects assigned to δόξα, the capacity itself, and the position between being and not-being.
δοξαστόν appears first as the goal of the search at 478e, then returns at 479d explicitly contrasted with γνωστόν.

elements.context: δοξάζειν φήσομεν ἅπαντα, γιγνώσκειν δὲ ὧν δοξάζουσιν οὐδέν
ἆρʼ οὐ γιγνώσκειν ἀλλʼ οὐ δοξάζειν

signals.observation: δοξάζειν and γιγνώσκειν are set in direct opposition twice in close succession at 479e, with their positions reversed between the two groups described.
θεάομαι is used for both groups—those viewing many beautifuls and those viewing each thing itself—then returns at 480a for the lovers of sights and sounds.

elements.context: φιλοδόξους καλοῦντες αὐτοὺς μᾶλλον ἢ φιλοσόφους

signals.observation: φιλόδοξος and φιλόσοφος are placed in direct contrast as rival designations at the section's close.

elements.context: καλά πως αὐτὰ καὶ αἰσχρὰ φανῆναι

signals.observation: Three value-pairs (καλόν/αἰσχρόν, δίκαιον/ἄδικον, ὅσιον/ἀνόσιον) are cited as cases where each many appears as its own opposite.
A cluster of relative-quantity and relative-quality opposites (double/half, great/small, light/heavy) extends the argument from value-terms to quantitative predicates.
ἐπαμφοτερίζω appears twice, first for the riddling double-meanings at feasts and then applied to the many beautifuls themselves.
The riddle of the eunuch and the bat is introduced as an analogy for things that cannot be stably conceived as either being or not-being.
σκοτωδέστερα and φανότερα are set as the limits between which the many beautifuls fall—darker than not-being and brighter than being are both denied.

elements.context: μεταξύ που κυλινδεῖται τοῦ τε μὴ ὄντος καὶ τοῦ ὄντος

signals.observation: κυλινδεῖται and πλανητόν characterize the many conventionals with images of rolling and wandering between being and not-being.

elements.context: αὐτὸ ἄρα ἕκαστον τὸ ὂν ἀσπαζομένους

signals.observation: ἀσπάζομαι first appears alongside φιλεῖν for those who welcome objects of knowledge, then returns at 480a applied specifically to those who welcome each being itself.

The φιλ- prefix recurs across the section: the interlocutor is first called φιλοθεάμων, then φιλεῖν describes his attachment, and finally the naming contest φιλόδοξος vs. φιλόσοφος resolves the characterization.
εὑρεῖν is proposed as what remains to be found at 478e; ηὑρήκαμεν at 479d declares the finding accomplished.
εἰλικρινής appears at 478e denying purity to the intermediate object and returns at 479d denying it pure being.

elements.context: τῷ γὰρ ἀληθεῖ χαλεπαίνειν οὐ θέμις

signals.observation: χαλεπαίνω appears twice in immediate succession: first as the anticipated anger of the opinion-lovers, then denied as lawful (θέμις) when directed at truth.
